page1.text:
The swordsman holds up his sword.
An unknown, imaginary stance for an unknown, imaginary man.
He readies his fatal technique that cuts his enemy by simultaneously executing blows from different angles.
She's experienced that attack before.
The previous one only attacked in a circular motion and at a vertical axis.
That was why she was able to avoid it and managed to survive.

page2.text:
But the true technique is said to have three trajectories.
A circular and vertical slash...and probably a horizontal slash that cuts anyone who tries to escape sideways.
If all three of those were to be released simultaneously, there is no escape.
Once in range, the other two attacks will hit even if one is blocked.
Escaping sideways is impossible, and the long katana will be able to make contact if the target tries to retreat back.

page3.text:
Magical sword, Swallow Reversal.
A divine technique that surpasses even the powers of Servants.
This is the ultimate technique an unknown swordsman put his entire existence in perfecting.

page4.text:
The long katana wavers.
He steps in to reduce the distance between the opponents.
A distance close enough to cut down Saber.
From a distance that does not allow any defense, a constricting trajectory is unleashed.

page5.text:
...
Saber is not going to use her sacred sword.
To begin with, she can't use her Noble Phantasm from the distance the two are at.
No matter how fast Saber's sacred sword may be, Assassin's Swallow Reversal is much faster.
Her head will surely fly while she tries to put magical energy in her sword.
Thus, the only thing she can rely on is her sword skills.

page6.text:
The blade's arc begins to move in.
Even though this is her second time seeing it, its precision and speed are astonishing.
How much training did he do to be able to execute an attack like that?

page7.text:
...
At that moment, Saber could only shudder.
That attack cannot be blocked.
This magical sword is man's attempt at challenging the gods and Buddha.
Nobody but a god would be able to prevent or parry the attack.

page8.text:
"Ha...h..."
She holds her breath.
In the back of her mind, there is a faint spark as small as a grain of sand.
She doesn't think of what that is, or if it's the right thing to do.
But she risks everything on that one instinctual inspiration.
"Ah...!"
She charges towards that victory with all she has.

page9.text:
What did the fictional swordsmaster think in seeing that?
"...Kngh."
The silver armor slips through the gap between his arms.
Under the swordsman's left elbow, between his waist and arm.
She must have seen that the slightest gap was the magical sword's blind spot.

page10.text:
While her armor gets chipped away by the three blades that come flying, Saber curls herself up and rushes toward that one point.
Her prediction...her outstanding intuition allows her to execute that exquisite skill.
She was able to foresee the complete form of the magical sword—which was yet to be seen—because she had experienced the incomplete Swallow Reversal once.

page11.text:
However, that is not the surprising thing.
What truly kept her alive was her determination.
She trusted that momentary spark, and put all of her abilities into that momentary gap.
She shook off the fear that she might get cut up into pieces if she was even slightly delayed, and ran through the gap that was impossible to pass.
And thus...
Her determination was what managed to defeat that magical blade.

page12.text:
"Ah...haaah!"
But the match is not over.
Avoiding the Swallow Reversal puts her enemy right next to her, and her lunge outpaces the swordsman's draw.
That position is not easy to recover from!

page13.text:
"Jyah...!"
The long katana flies.
The recoiling blade is quick, even if it may not be as quick as the demonic blade.
And yet...
Her attack slightly outperforms and is faster than the swordsman's.

page14.text:
"Ghn...nh!"
He purses his lips.
He closes his lips tightly and strains to keep himself from collapsing.
The blood that flows back from his gut fills his mouth, but he swallows it, determined not to spit it out.
The golden-haired knight stands below the swordsman.
The swordsman's code does not allow him to do something like defile his opponent and her brilliance with the expulsions from his innards.

page15.text:
...
Saber says nothing.
Strands of her golden hair flutter on to the stone stairs.
It's a wonder her head is still attached.
It's a miracle that her limbs were not sheared off.
She felt her body would be cut in four the instant she went into that opening.

page16.text:
There was only one factor that made a difference.
The swordsman's long katana.
Had his blade not bent, his magical sword would have surely been invincible.

page17.text:
The air is rumbling.
Another battle is still going on behind the temple gate.
"..."
Saber does not know what to say, as she looks up at the dying swordsman.
To that...

page18.text:
"Go..."
The swordsman says without looking at her.
How much meaning is contained in that single word?
Saber draws her sword and runs up the stairs with all her might.
She doesn't turn back to the swordsman.
She simply runs up to fulfill her role.

page19.text:
"Heh. I had thought she was a beautiful bird, but she turned out to be a lion."
He mutters, and the swordsman laughs realizing it was inevitable.
She avoided something that even a swallow could not avoid. And thus she was not an object to be admired and loved.

page20.text:
"Hm. I was confident in my ability to assess women. I suppose I require more training in that front as well."
The swordsman complains with a shrug.
His form and his elegant haori were starting to fade.
His pierced stomach and his bloodstained feet become faint.
Yet he looked at his situation unconcerned, and sat down on the stone pavement.
